title: Evaluation “Emotionslotse”: App-based support for emotion perception and regulation in everyday life using biocueing
summary:
This study evaluates the Emotionslotse app, a digital application designed to support emotion awareness and emotion regulation in everyday life. The app provides knowledge about emotions, offers guided exercises and includes an artificial-intelligence-based chatbot that supports participants in reflecting on emotional situations. In addition, a so-called biocueing approach is used: physiological data collected via a wearable device are used to trigger prompts in certain everyday situations. These prompts are intended to encourage participants to apply emotion regulation strategies they have previously learned.
This is a 30-day prospective study with a planned sample size of 100 mentally healthy adults. Before inclusion in the study, participants undergo screening to check the inclusion and exclusion criteria. At the beginning of the study, participants complete a baseline questionnaire, including questions on emotion regulation skills, perceived stress, depressive symptoms and attitudes toward artificial intelligence. During the four-week study phase, participants use the Emotionslotse app at least five times per week for approximately five minutes each time, wear a study-provided wearable device and complete weekly questionnaires on experienced emotions and their perception of the biocueing prompts. After 30 days, participants complete a final follow-up questionnaire assessing emotion regulation, acceptance, usability, perceived benefit and technology-related experiences.
The primary aim of the study is to investigate whether use of the Emotionslotse app is associated with improved emotion regulation skills and increased use of learned strategies in everyday life. Further aims are to assess the app’s acceptance, practicality and usability, and to evaluate the extent to which wearable-based prompts can support the use of emotion regulation strategies in everyday life. The study evaluates a preventive digital support tool and does not constitute a medical treatment procedure.

interventions.name: Single-arm prospective observational group: After screening, study information and informed consent, all included participants receive access to the Emotionslotse app and a wearable device. Participants use the Emotionslotse app for 4 weeks or 30 days at least five times per week for 5 minutes each

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Sex/gender: male, female, diverse
Minimum age: 18 years
Sufficient German language skills
Ownership of a compatible smartphone
Willingness to wear a wearable device for 30 days, use the Emotionslotse app and complete app-based questionnaires
Willingness and ability to attend the study centre in Leipzig
Written or documented informed consent after study information has been provided
Exclusion criteria:
Age under 18 years
Pregnancy
Presence of a diagnosed mental disorder or current treatment for a mental disorder
Moderate or severe depressive or anxiety-related symptoms at screening, operationalised as PHQ-4 > 5
Moderate or severe psychological distress at screening, operationalised as K10 > 25
Missing information at screening on any of the relevant inclusion or exclusion criteria
